cultural.vision_reason: The picture shows a Fon appliqué banner depicting Dahomean warriors and their victory over the Yoruba. It is identified as made by Fon artists and is a characteristic traditional Fon textile.

physical.title: banner
physical.summary: Banner with a buff background onto which have been appliqued cut-out pieces of textile of various colours. The composition depicts the victory of the Dahomian warriors in the time of King Glele (1858-89) over their Yoruba enemies.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Cloth formed of eight narrow strips hand-woven and hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The material used is raffia and handspun cotton, which has either been left white or has been dyed dark indigo. The warp in all the strips is a light-coloured raffia. The cloth is dominated by a pattern of six blocks, each framing an white centre. The sides of the blocks are formed by using indigo rather than white thread in the weft. In the centre of each block are small bundles of what appears to be imported European thread dyed red, green and blue, used as supplementary weft decoration; the form of these motifs varies. The warp ends have been hemmed.
